match.reason: The bank's influence points cover how economic, social and technological forces affect a business generally at Year 11, while this point is specifically about how they change employment and the management of staff, such as part-time and remote work, so it is a narrower human resources idea.

draft.title: Economic, social and technological influences
card: Economic
The state of the economy affects hiring. In a downturn, businesses may freeze hiring, cut hours or retrench staff. In a boom, they compete for workers and may offer higher pay.
Social
Work patterns change as society does. More people work part-time, casually or from home, and many want flexible hours. Businesses may respond with flexible rosters and remote work options.
Technological
New technology changes the tasks people do and the skills they need. Some routine jobs may be automated, so businesses may retrain staff or hire people with new skills.
These influences sit outside the HR manager's control, but managers must adjust how they recruit, train, reward and organise staff to respond to them.
draft.remember: Economic, social and technological change all push a business to adjust how it employs and manages people.

a.q: Demand for Leila's tourism business falls sharply in a downturn. Which HR response is an economic influence at work?
opts: Freezing hiring and cutting staff hours
Offering staff the option to work from home
Training staff to use new booking software
Changing rosters so parents can pick up children
a.why: A fall in demand caused by the state of the economy leads to a hiring freeze and cuts to hours. The other options respond to social or technological change, and the remote work option is tempting but is not caused by the economy.
a.clue: Which response is caused by weaker spending in the economy?

b.q: A Newcastle accounting firm adopts software that completes routine data entry automatically. It retrains its data entry staff as client advisers. Which influence is mainly shown?
opts: Technological, as new tools change the skills needed
Economic, as a downturn forces the firm to cut costs
Social, as staff now want more flexible work patterns
Economic, as a boom leads the firm to raise pay
b.why: The change begins with new software that automates routine tasks, so the firm retrains staff for new skills. This is a technological influence. Cost cutting is tempting, but the case describes no downturn and no staff losses.
b.clue: What started the change: the economy, society or a new tool?

a.best: Freezing hiring and cutting staff hours

b.best: Technological, as new tools change the skills needed
